addition__kindergarten.title: Addition Worksheets for Kindergarten – Free PDF
addition__kindergarten.metaDescription: Free printable addition worksheets for kindergarten: picture addition and sums to 10 with cheerful themes. Download PDFs with answer keys or solve them online.
addition__kindergarten.prose:
Kindergarten addition starts with things a child can see and count, and these addition worksheets for kindergarten keep every problem that concrete. On each row a first group of pictures is shown, and the child counts them, looks at the total for the row, and works out how many more belong in the empty box beside them. Because both the parts and the whole are pictured, a five- or six-year-old can count up to the answer instead of recalling a fact they have not learned yet. Every sum stays within ten, which is exactly the range kindergarten works in.

Some sheets show two full groups to join and count all together for a plain sums-to-ten problem; others leave one group blank so the child finds the missing addend. Cheerful themes -- animals, food, vehicles -- make the counting feel like play rather than drill. A teacher can hand the page out at a math station, and a parent can sit beside a child at the kitchen table and count the pictures together.

Everything here is free, with no sign-up of any kind. Print any of more than 200 kindergarten addition sets as a PDF, print the matching answer key to check the work in seconds, or open the very same worksheet online and let the child tap out each answer on a tablet.

kindergarten__subtraction.title: Subtraction Worksheets for Kindergarten – Free PDF
kindergarten__subtraction.metaDescription: Free printable subtraction worksheets for kindergarten: cross out pictures and take away within 10. Every set has a PDF, an answer key and an online version.
kindergarten__subtraction.prose:
Subtraction in kindergarten is something a child does with their hands long before it becomes a written symbol, and these subtraction worksheets for kindergarten are built exactly that way. Each row shows a group of pictures and asks the child to cross some of them out, then write how many are left. Crossing-out is the heart of it: the child physically removes the ones that go away and counts the ones that remain, so take-away feels real. Every problem stays within ten, the range a kindergartner is ready for.

Because the pictures carry the whole problem, a child who cannot yet read an equation can still solve every line -- they count, cross out, and count again. A few sheets turn it around and ask how many are missing from a group, which is the gentle first step toward finding a missing number. Friendly themes keep the mood light, and the big, clear pictures leave room for little fingers to mark each one out.

Use the page however suits you. Print it as a PDF for a quiet morning task, print the answer key so checking takes a moment, or play the identical worksheet online where crossing out is a tap. There are more than 200 kindergarten subtraction sets to choose from, all completely free and open to everyone with no account and no login.

kindergarten__missing-pieces.metaDescription: Free missing parts worksheets for kindergarten: spot which piece completes each picture and snap it into place. Printable PDFs plus a play-online mode.
kindergarten__missing-pieces.prose:
This missing parts practice asks one simple question: what is missing from the picture? These missing parts worksheets for kindergarten show a picture with one piece cut away, leaving a clear gap, and a small set of choices below. The child studies the shape of the hole, imagines the whole picture put back together, and picks the piece that completes it. There is nothing to read and nothing to count -- it is pure looking and reasoning.

Working out which piece belongs is whole-and-part thinking, a readiness skill kindergartners build by noticing how things fit together. It also trains careful attention: the wrong pieces are close enough that a child has to compare shapes and edges rather than grab the first option. Familiar themes -- animals, food, toys -- keep every picture easy to recognize, so the only real puzzle is the missing part.

With nearly 300 sets on hand, a teacher can pull a fresh page for a puzzle center every day, and a parent has plenty for a rainy afternoon. Print any worksheet as a PDF, print its answer key to confirm the right choice at a glance, or open the same puzzle online and let the child tap the piece that fits. Everything is free for everyone, with no sign-up, no subscription, and no limit on how many you use.

kindergarten__picture-sort.prose:
Sorting is one of the first real thinking moves a young child makes, and these picture sorting worksheets for kindergarten give plenty of practice at it. Each page mixes two kinds of pictures together -- say a handful of animals jumbled in with a handful of birds -- and asks the child to put each one where it belongs. Deciding which group a picture fits is early classifying: the child notices what makes things alike or different and groups them by that idea. There is no counting, just looking and grouping.

Some sheets are meant to be dragged and dropped online; the printable versions work beautifully as cut-and-paste, where a child snips each picture and glues it under the right heading. That physical sorting suits a kindergarten classroom station and busy little hands. The categories stay concrete and familiar -- kinds of animals, kinds of food, things that go -- so a five-year-old can reason it out on their own.

There are more than 240 picture sort sets here, enough for a new one every week of the year. Print a worksheet as a PDF, print the answer key so you can check the groups quickly, or play the same sort online with a tap-to-place tablet version. It is all free, with no account required and nothing hidden behind a paywall -- pick a page and let the sorting begin.

more-less__preschool.prose:
Long before a child can count reliably, they can look at two bunches of things and feel which one has more, and these more or less worksheets for preschool grow exactly that sense. Each page shows two groups of pictures side by side and asks the child to point to the group with more -- or on some rows, the group with fewer. There is no counting required; the whole task is the quick, at-a-glance comparison that is one of a young child's very first quantity ideas.

For ages three to five, the pictures stay large and the groups small, so the difference is easy to see and the child can answer with confidence. Comparing two amounts and choosing more or fewer builds the foundation that later counting and adding will stand on. Familiar, cheerful pictures keep every page inviting, and there is no reading anywhere on the sheet.

With more than 150 preschool sets to pull from, there is always a fresh page for circle time or a one-on-one moment at home. Print any worksheet as a PDF, print its answer key so you can check the choice instantly, or open the same activity online where the child taps the bigger group. grade-1__math-puzzle.prose:
By first grade a child is ready for math that feels like a real puzzle, and these math puzzles for 1st grade turn addition into a game. Each page is a crossword-style grid of small sums, where the numbers along every row and every column have to add up correctly. The child solves one cell, checks it against its neighbours, and adjusts until the whole grid balances. Every calculation stays within twenty, right in the first-grade fluency range.

The pleasure of it is that the puzzle checks itself: a wrong answer throws off a row or a column, so the grid quietly tells a child where to look again. That makes it far more engaging than a page of isolated problems, and it builds real number sense as a child juggles several small sums at once.
